title: Power Tower Integrality: Lean Proof Program
problem: Prove N = π^(π^(π^π)) ∉ ℤ via topological/analytic methods
current_status: Analytical computation only (0.31766...); all topology is decorative
theorem: N = π^(π^(π^π)) is transcendental and its fractional part {log log log log N} ≈ 0.31766 ≠ 0

G1_manifold_construction.issue: No actual manifold whose topology encodes the tower arithmetic
G1_manifold_construction.required: A space M with π₂(M) ≅ ℤ⁴ where Chern numbers = tower logs

G2_integer_invariant.issue: Intersection invariant is heuristic product, not proven invariant
G2_integer_invariant.required: Prove ∃ invariant I(M) ∈ ℤ such that I(M) = 0 ⇔ N ∈ ℤ

G3_monte_carlo.issue: MC estimates arbitrary function, not {log log log log N}
G3_monte_carlo.current: Samples random sphere points → norm mod 1
G3_monte_carlo.required: MC estimator that provably converges to {log log log log N}

G4_curvature_assignment.required: Curvatures derived from tower arithmetic (Baker/Schanuel theory)

G5_tower_manifold_map.current: Log-space vector → exp map on arbitrary spheres
G5_tower_manifold_map.required: Explicit homeomorphism between tower log-space and M

phase_1_analytic_foundation.title: Phase 1: Analytic Foundation (Weeks 1-2)
goals: Rigorously compute fractional part to 50+ decimal places (MPFR)
Prove {log log log log N} = f(π) where f is explicit analytic function
Establish error bounds for all finite-precision computations
Derive exact expression: {log log log log π^(π^(π^π))} = g(π) where g is computable

results.note: mpmath not available; used standard math library with double precision

phase_2_baker_schanuel_connection.title: Phase 2: Baker/Schanuel Connection (Weeks 3-6)
goals: Express log N as linear form in logarithms: log N = Σ aᵢ log bᵢ
Apply Baker's theorem to bound |log N - nearest integer|
If Schanuel's conjecture assumed: prove transcendence directly
Connect fractional part to linear form distance from integers
phase_2_baker_schanuel_connection.note: This is the standard analytic approach; topology is optional here

phase_3_topological_lift.title: Phase 3: Topological Lift (Weeks 7-12) - RESEARCH LEVEL
goals: Construct manifold M = iterated S²-bundle over S¹ with connection
Connection form A = (ln π, π ln π, π² ln π, π³ ln π) in Lie algebra
Chern-Weil theory: c₁(F_A) = (i/2π) Tr(F_A ∧ F_A) gives integer invariants
Prove: fractional part = Chern number mod 1 + exponentially small error
This is the "real" topological attack - requires new math
phase_3_topological_lift.risk: May require new mathematics; no guarantee of success

phase_4_computational_certificate.title: Phase 4: Computational Certificate (Weeks 13-16)
goals: Verified by independent interval arithmetic libraries (Arb, MPFI)
Formal proof in Lean 4 or Coq (optional but ideal)

what_works_now: Baker's theorem gives explicit lower bound on |log N - integer|
MPFR interval arithmetic can produce formal certificate
what_is_research: Topological lift (Phase 3) - may be impossible or require new theory
Chern-Weil connection to fractional part - unproven conjecture
Any topological proof that avoids Baker/Schanuel is likely harder
realistic_assessment.recommended_path: Phase 1 + 2 + 4 = complete rigorous certificate; Phase 3 = separate research project
